institution_standard: AICTE / Model University B.Tech Engineering Curriculum

key_formulas: Characteristic Equation: |A - λI| = 0
Cayley-Hamilton: P(A) = 0 where P(λ) is the characteristic polynomial
Inverse via Cayley-Hamilton: A^(-1) = -(1/a_0)(A^(n-1) + a_(n-1)A^(n-2) + ... + a_1 I)
Rank-Nullity Theorem: Rank(A) + Nullity(A) = n
canonical_problem_types: Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a 3x3 matrix
Verify Cayley-Hamilton Theorem for matrix A and find A^(-1) and A^4
Determine consistency and find solutions of AX = B
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Set up characteristic determinant det(A - λI) = 0
Step 2: Expand characteristic polynomial correctly without sign errors
Step 3: Solve polynomial for eigenvalues λ_1, λ_2, λ_3
Step 4: Solve (A - λ_i I)X = 0 to extract non-trivial eigenvectors
Step 5: Normalize and state linearly independent vectors
common_misconceptions: Sign errors in determinant cofactor expansion
Confusing eigenvalue roots with matrix diagonal elements
Claiming non-invertible matrix has no eigenvalues

standard_topics: Taylor Series for Functions of Two Variables
key_formulas: Euler's Theorem: x(∂u/∂x) + y(∂u/∂y) = n*u
Jacobian: J(u,v / x,y) = (∂u/∂x)(∂v/∂y) - (∂u/∂y)(∂v/∂x)
Extrema Test: D = rt - s^2 where r = ∂²f/∂x², s = ∂²f/∂x∂y, t = ∂²f/∂y² (D > 0, r > 0 => Min; D > 0, r < 0 => Max; D < 0 => Saddle)
canonical_problem_types: Examine extreme values of f(x, y) = x³ + y³ - 3axy
Find maxima/minima subject to constraint g(x, y) = 0 using Lagrange multipliers
Verify Euler's theorem for u = tan^(-1)((x³+y³)/(x-y))
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Calculate first partial derivatives fx = 0, fy = 0
Step 2: Solve simultaneous equations to find critical points (x_0, y_0)
Step 3: Calculate second partial derivatives r = fxx, s = fxy, t = fyy
Step 4: Evaluate discriminant D = rt - s² at each critical point
Step 5: Conclude whether point is Local Maximum, Local Minimum, or Saddle Point
common_misconceptions: Forgetting to check the sign of r when D > 0
Treating D < 0 as inconclusive instead of Saddle Point

standard_topics: Double Integrals in Cartesian & Polar Coordinates
key_formulas: Change of Variables: dx dy = |J| dr dθ = r dr dθ
Gauss Divergence: ∬_S F·n dS = ∭_V (∇·F) dV
Stokes' Theorem: ∮_C F·dr = ∬_S (∇×F)·n dS
Beta-Gamma Relation: B(m, n) = (Γ(m)Γ(n)) / Γ(m+n)
canonical_problem_types: Evaluate integral by changing the order of integration
Verify Gauss Divergence theorem for F = (x)i + (y)j + (z)k over a cylinder
Verify Stokes theorem for a vector field along a closed boundary
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Sketch region of integration and write boundary equations
Step 2: Determine new limits after changing integration order
Step 3: Compute inner integral holding outer variable constant
Step 4: Compute outer integral and verify dimensional consistency
common_misconceptions: Changing order without adjusting dependent integration limits
Omitting the Jacobian r in polar transformations dx dy = r dr dθ

key_formulas: Thin Film Constructive: 2μt cos(r) = (2n - 1)(λ/2)
Newton's Rings Dark Ring Diameter: D_n² = 4n R λ
Grating Equation: (a + b) sin(θ) = n λ
Brewster's Law: μ = tan(θ_p)
canonical_problem_types: Calculate radius of curvature of lens using Newton's rings dark ring diameters
Determine thickness of thin wire using wedge-shaped interference fringes
Find wavelengths of spectral lines using plane diffraction grating
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: State path difference formula with Stokes phase shift λ/2
Step 2: Relate film thickness t to ring diameter D_n and lens radius R
Step 3: Substitute measured diameters D_(n+p)² - D_n² = 4 p R λ
Step 4: Solve for unknown wavelength or radius with proper units (meters)
common_misconceptions: Neglecting phase change of π (path difference λ/2) on reflection at denser medium
Confusing fringe width with ring radius

standard_topics: Particle in a 1D Infinite Potential Well
key_formulas: de Broglie Wavelength: λ = h / p = h / √(2mE)
Heisenberg: Δx * Δp ≥ ℏ / 2
Schrödinger Equation: - (ℏ² / 2m) (d²ψ/dx²) + V ψ = E ψ
1D Box Eigenenergies: E_n = (n² h²) / (8 m L²)
1D Box Eigenfunctions: ψ_n(x) = √(2/L) sin(n π x / L)
canonical_problem_types: Derive energy eigenvalues for a particle in a 1D rigid box of width L
Calculate zero-point energy of an electron in a 1 nm well
Evaluate probability of finding particle in interval [0, L/4]
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Set up boundary conditions ψ(0) = 0 and ψ(L) = 0
Step 2: Solve second order ODE to get ψ(x) = A sin(kx) + B cos(kx)
Step 3: Apply boundary conditions to find B = 0 and k = nπ/L
Step 4: Relate wave vector k to energy: E = ℏ²k² / (2m)
Step 5: Normalize wavefunction ∫|ψ|² dx = 1 to find amplitude A = √(2/L)
common_misconceptions: Setting ground state quantum number n = 0 (n must start at 1)
Assuming zero-point energy is zero (it is h²/(8mL²))

standard_topics: Optical Fiber Numerical Aperture & Acceptance Angle
key_formulas: Einstein Ratio: A_21 / B_21 = (8 π h ν³) / c³
Numerical Aperture: NA = √(n_core² - n_cladding²) = sin(θ_a)
Acceptance Angle: θ_a = sin^(-1)(√(n_core² - n_cladding²))
Fermi-Dirac Distribution: f(E) = 1 / (1 + exp((E - E_F) / (k_B T)))
canonical_problem_types: Calculate acceptance angle and numerical aperture of an optical fiber
Determine ratio of stimulated to spontaneous emission at given temperature
Find position of Fermi level in n-type semiconductor at 300 K
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Apply Snell's law at fiber entrance face
Step 2: Apply total internal reflection condition at core-cladding boundary (sin φ ≥ n2/n1)
Step 3: Relate internal angle to external acceptance angle
Step 4: Formulate NA = √(n1² - n2²)
common_misconceptions: Assuming core refractive index can be lower than cladding (n1 must > n2)
Inverting Einstein coefficient ratio

key_formulas: Nernst Equation: E = E° - (RT / nF) ln(Q) = E° - (0.0591 / n) log10(Q) at 298K
Gibbs-Helmholtz: ΔG = ΔH - T ΔS = - n F E_cell
Corrosion Rate (Faraday): W = (I * t * M) / (n * F)
canonical_problem_types: Calculate EMF of electrochemical cell at 298 K using Nernst equation
Determine free energy change ΔG° and equilibrium constant K_eq
Explain rusting of iron with anodic and cathodic electrochemical reactions
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Identify anode (oxidation) and cathode (reduction) half-reactions
Step 2: Calculate standard cell potential E°cell = E°cathode - E°anode
Step 3: Formulate reaction quotient Q = [Products] / [Reactants]
Step 4: Substitute into Nernst formula E = E° - (0.0591/n) log(Q)
Step 5: Compute cell potential and verify spontaneity (E > 0 => ΔG < 0)
common_misconceptions: Reversing anode and cathode in standard potential calculation
Including pure solids or liquids in reaction quotient Q

key_formulas: Total Hardness (ppm as CaCO3): (V_EDTA * M_EDTA * 100 * 1000) / V_water
Equivalent Weight of CaCO3: 50 g/eq (Molecular Weight = 100 g/mol)
canonical_problem_types: Calculate temporary, permanent, and total hardness from EDTA titration data
Design ion-exchange resin capacity for given water flow rate
Distinguish addition and condensation polymerization with examples
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Balance EDTA-metal 1:1 complex stoichiometry
Step 2: Calculate molarity of EDTA from standard hard water titration
Step 3: Calculate CaCO3 equivalents in sample
Step 4: Express total hardness in parts per million (ppm or mg/L)
common_misconceptions: Confusing molecular weight (100) with equivalent weight (50) of CaCO3
Attributing permanent hardness to bicarbonates instead of chlorides/sulfates

standard_topics: Functions & Parameter Passing (Call by Value / Reference)
Recursive Functions (Tower of Hanoi, Fibonacci, Factorial)
key_formulas: Recursion Invariant: Base Case termination condition mandatory
Time Complexity: T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1 for Tower of Hanoi (O(2^n))
canonical_problem_types: Write recursive C function for Tower of Hanoi and trace call stack for n=3
Implement iterative and recursive binary search on sorted array
Explain call by value versus call by reference with swap function
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Declare function prototypes with correct parameter types
Step 2: Define base case condition to prevent infinite stack overflow
Step 3: Define recursive reduction step
Step 4: Trace activation records on runtime stack
common_misconceptions: Omitting base case causing segmentation fault / stack overflow
Expecting call by value to mutate caller variables

standard_topics: Pointers to Arrays & Arrays of Pointers
Dynamic Memory Allocation (malloc, calloc, realloc, free)
File Handling Operations (fopen, fread, fwrite, fclose)
key_formulas: Array Indexing Address: *(arr + i) == arr[i]
2D Row-Major Address: Base + (i * cols + j) * sizeof(type)
Memory Deallocation: free(ptr); ptr = NULL; to prevent dangling pointers
canonical_problem_types: Implement matrix multiplication with dimension compatibility check
Allocate dynamic 2D array using double pointers (int **)
Create a student record database using structures and binary files
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Check matrix compatibility: columns of A must equal rows of B
Step 2: Allocate dynamic memory and check for NULL return
Step 3: Execute triple nested loop with accumulator initialized to 0
Step 4: Free allocated blocks in reverse order
common_misconceptions: Failing to check if malloc returned NULL
Using pointer after free (dangling pointer)

key_formulas: KVL: ∑ V = 0, KCL: ∑ I_in = ∑ I_out
Thevenin Voltage: V_th = Open Circuit Voltage across terminals A-B
Thevenin Resistance: R_th = Equivalent resistance with independent sources killed (Voltage -> short, Current -> open)
Max Power Condition: R_L = R_th => P_max = V_th² / (4 R_th)
canonical_problem_types: Find current through load resistor using Thevenin theorem
Verify Superposition theorem in a multi-source circuit
Determine maximum power transferred to variable load resistor R_L
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Remove load resistor R_L to identify terminals A and B
Step 2: Calculate open-circuit voltage V_th using mesh or nodal analysis
Step 3: Deactivate independent sources (short voltage, open current)
Step 4: Calculate equivalent resistance R_th looking into terminals A-B
Step 5: Connect Thevenin equivalent circuit and compute I_L = V_th / (R_th + R_L)
common_misconceptions: Deactivating dependent sources (dependent sources must NOT be killed)
Leaving voltage sources as open circuits instead of short circuits

modules.module_title: Linear Data Structures: Stacks, Queues & Linked Lists
standard_topics: Stack Implementation & Infix to Postfix Conversion
Queue Implementation (Circular Queue, Deque, Priority Queue)
key_formulas: Circular Queue Next Position: rear = (rear + 1) % capacity
Master Theorem: T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n)
canonical_problem_types: Convert given infix expression to postfix using stack algorithm
Implement circular queue operations handling overflow and underflow
Reverse a singly linked list in O(n) time and O(1) space
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Initialize operator stack and output buffer
Step 2: Process tokens respecting operator precedence and associativity
Step 3: Pop higher/equal precedence operators to output on encountering operator
Step 4: Unwind stack to output on end of string
common_misconceptions: Confusing operator precedence between multiplication/division and addition/subtraction
Neglecting boundary case when queue is full in circular array

standard_topics: AVL Trees & Rotations (LL, RR, LR, RL)
key_formulas: AVL Balance Factor: BF = Height(LeftSubtree) - Height(RightSubtree) ∈ {-1, 0, +1}
Dijkstra Relaxation: if dist[u] + weight(u, v) < dist[v] then dist[v] = dist[u] + weight(u, v)
0/1 Knapsack DP: dp[i][w] = max(dp[i-1][w], dp[i-1][w - w_i] + v_i)
canonical_problem_types: Construct an AVL tree for a sequence of numbers showing rotation steps
Find minimum spanning tree cost using Prim's algorithm with priority queue
Solve 0/1 knapsack problem using dynamic programming table
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Set up DP recurrence relations and boundary conditions
Step 2: Construct 2D DP matrix filling row by row
Step 3: Compute optimal value at dp[N][W]
Step 4: Trace back selected items through DP table
common_misconceptions: Applying greedy fractional strategy to 0/1 knapsack (items cannot be divided)
Allowing negative edge weights in Dijkstra's algorithm

standard_topics: CPU Scheduling (FCFS, SJF, Round Robin, Priority)
key_formulas: Turnaround Time: TAT = Completion Time - Arrival Time
Waiting Time: WT = Turnaround Time - Burst Time
Banker's Safety: Need[i][j] = Max[i][j] - Allocation[i][j] ≤ Work[j]
canonical_problem_types: Draw Gantt chart and calculate average turnaround and waiting times for Round Robin (quantum=2)
Apply Banker's algorithm to determine if system state is safe and find safe sequence
Implement reader-writer synchronization using counting and binary semaphores
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Compute Need matrix = Max - Allocation for all processes
Step 2: Initialize Work = Available and Finish = all false
Step 3: Find process P_i where Finish[i] == false and Need[i] ≤ Work
Step 4: Reclaim resources Work = Work + Allocation[i], set Finish[i] = true
Step 5: Output complete safe sequence if all finish, else declare unsafe
common_misconceptions: Assuming unsafe state is identical to deadlock (unsafe state may lead to deadlock, but is not yet deadlocked)
Forgetting to subtract arrival time when calculating waiting time

modules.module_title: First & Second Laws of Thermodynamics & Cycles
standard_topics: First Law for Closed & Open Systems (Steady Flow Energy Equation)
Entropy Change in Reversible & Irreversible Processes
key_formulas: SFEE: q - w = Δh + Δ(v²/2) + gΔz
Carnot Efficiency: η_th = 1 - (T_L / T_H) where T is absolute temperature in Kelvin
Clausius Inequality: ∮ (dQ / T) ≤ 0
Entropy Change of Ideal Gas: Δs = c_p ln(T2/T1) - R ln(P2/P1)
canonical_problem_types: Calculate thermal efficiency and power output of a Carnot engine operating between 800 K and 300 K
Determine entropy generation in an irreversible heat transfer process
Evaluate steam cycle efficiency using Rankine cycle with superheat
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Convert temperatures to Kelvin (T_K = T_C + 273.15)
Step 2: Formulate energy conservation balance Q_in - Q_out = W_net
Step 3: Calculate ideal efficiency η = 1 - T_L / T_H
Step 4: Compute actual work output W = η * Q_in
common_misconceptions: Using temperatures in Celsius instead of Kelvin in Carnot formula
Neglecting heat rejected to sink Q_out when calculating work

key_formulas: Convolution: y(t) = ∫ x(τ) h(t - τ) dτ
Fourier Transform: X(ω) = ∫ x(t) e^(-jωt) dt
Z-Transform: X(z) = ∑ x[n] z^(-n)
LTI Stability: System is BIBO stable if ROC contains unit circle |z| = 1
canonical_problem_types: Determine convolution of two rectangular pulse signals
Find Z-transform and ROC of x[n] = a^n u[n] - b^n u[-n-1]
Test LTI system for linearity, time-invariance, and causality
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Check linearity: T{a x1 + b x2} = a T{x1} + b T{x2}
Step 2: Check time-invariance: T{x(t - t0)} = y(t - t0)
Step 3: Check causality: output y(t) depends only on current and past inputs
Step 4: State rigorous mathematical conclusion
common_misconceptions: Confusing time reversal x(-t) with time shifting x(t - t0)
Neglecting Region of Convergence (ROC) when specifying Z-transform

standard_topics: Time Response of Second-Order Systems (Damping Ratio, Natural Frequency)
Root Locus Technique & Frequency Response (Bode Plots)
key_formulas: Second Order Transfer Function: G(s) = ω_n² / (s² + 2ζω_n s + ω_n²)
Damped Frequency: ω_d = ω_n √(1 - ζ²)
Peak Overshoot: %M_p = exp(- (π ζ) / √(1 - ζ²)) * 100
Settling Time (2% criterion): t_s = 4 / (ζ ω_n)
canonical_problem_types: Find transfer function of feedback system using block diagram reduction
Determine stability and number of right-half plane poles using Routh array
Calculate rise time, peak overshoot, and settling time for step input
expected_derivation_steps: Step 1: Set up characteristic equation 1 + G(s)H(s) = 0
Step 2: Construct Routh table array row by row
Step 3: Inspect first column elements for sign changes
Step 4: Number of sign changes equals number of poles in right-half s-plane (unstable poles)
common_misconceptions: Treating a zero in the first column as stable without epsilon replacement
Forgetting that any sign change indicates instability
